Article Title: No active local militants in Kashmir Valley, but hunt for 65 Pakistani terrorists underway: Report
Article Text:
File photo: Army personnel patrol near the Line of Control (LoC), Jammu and Kashmir (Picture credit: PTI)

LeT, JeM account for majority of foreign terrorists

Lateef Bhat's killing ended search for last known active local militant

Security agencies cite decline in active terrorists

NEW DELHI: Security forces have launched a massive hunt for an estimated 65 Pakistani terrorists operating in Jammu and Kashmir , days after the killing of the last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir Valley, officials in the security establishment said.The 65 foreign terrorists are believed to have links with banned outfits, primarily the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), officials told news agency ANI.Of these, 35 are linked to the LeT and 25 to the JeM, while the remaining terrorists are associated with other outlawed groups.Their presence has been confirmed through inputs received by different intelligence agencies, and their movements are being monitored, officials said. However, the estimated figure may change as the terrorists frequently shift locations.The hunt comes after the killing of LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on November 18. His death left the Union Territory with no listed active local militants, according to the security establishment.Officials said the estimated number of terrorists operating in Jammu and Kashmir had declined from 91 in 2024, which included both local and foreign militants, to around 65 at present, comprising only Pakistani terrorists.According to the security establishment, most of the 65 foreign terrorists are affiliated with the LeT and the JeM. Both Pakistan-based outfits have been linked to major attacks in India, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2016 Uri attack and the 2019 Pulwama bombing.Officials said the foreign terrorists continued to operate in parts of Jammu and Kashmir, particularly in remote areas of the Jammu region. Districts such as Poonch, Rajouri, Kishtwar and Doda remain among the areas where their presence is being monitored.The rugged terrain and dense forests in these districts pose challenges for security operations, officials indicated. They added that the figure of 65 was based on assessments by multiple agencies and could fluctuate as the terrorists moved between locations.The disappearance of active local militants has changed the security landscape in the Valley, but security agencies continue to focus on preventing infiltration, identifying support networks and tracking foreign terrorists.Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces in Kulgam on November 18, following an eight-day search operation.The 22-year-old LeT terrorist was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long pursuit. His associate, Nisar, a new recruit, had been killed near Larnoo bypass on November 16.The operation followed an attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam on November 11, in which three personnel were injured. Security forces used human intelligence, CCTV footage and cyber surveillance to track Bhat, who had escaped an earlier encounter.Security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including through a video call and with the help of members of the mosque committee. He refused and was killed while attempting to escape the cordon.Jammu and Kashmir Police director General Nalin Prabhat had described the killing as a milestone in the fight against terrorism, saying local recruitment had fallen to almost zero.The latest assessment indicates a decline in the overall number of active terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir over recent years.According to ANI, 135 terrorists were active in the Union Territory in 2022, including 85 foreign terrorists and 50 local militants. The number further declined in 2023.The security establishment said intensified counter-terrorism operations had contributed to the reduction in the number of active militants. Officials indicated that multi-agency operations would continue to target the remaining foreign terrorists.They cited the elimination of all seven members of a JeM group led by Saifullah in Kishtwar earlier this year as an example of such operations.The group had infiltrated in April 2024 and was neutralised in a series of operations that culminated on February 22 in the Chatroo area during Operation Trashi-I.Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha has also expressed confidence that the region would soon become terror-free.Addressing a passing-out parade at the Sher-i-Kashmir Police Academy in Udhampur on November 18, he said only a handful of foreign terrorists remained in the Union Territory.Security agencies are continuing to monitor the situation, with a focus on tracking foreign militants, preventing cross-border infiltration and dismantling support networks operating in the region.
Article Summary: Security forces launch massive hunt for 65 Pakistani terrorists operating in Jammu and Kashmir. Hunt comes after killing of last known active local terrorist in Kashmir Valley. 65 foreign terrorists are believed to have links with banned outfits, primarily the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish- e-Mohammed (JeM)

Article Title: 'Will take Bangladesh by December 16': Bengal minister Arjun Singh vows revenge for killings of Hindus
Article Text:
Bengal minister vows to avenge killings of Hindus in neighbouring Bangladesh

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Arjun Singh has claimed that India would take over Bangladesh by December 16 and that the killings of Hindus in the neighbouring country would be "avenged", triggering fresh attention amid strained relations between the two countries.Speaking to reporters in Bhatpara on Tuesday, Singh made the remarks while referring to the killings of Hindus in Bangladesh. "We will take Bangladesh by December 16th. Enough is enough; there are no more excuses regarding Bangladesh. We will certainly take revenge for the way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh; there is no doubt about that," he said.His remarks came amid heightened tensions in Bangladesh over the proposed return of former Prime Minister and Awami League supremo Sheikh Hasina from India. Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kobir has said that Hasina would only be allowed to return as a "prisoner, in handcuffs" and under strict surveillance.Kobir reportedly made the remarks while speaking to journalists after briefing foreign diplomats at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka.Dismissing reports that Hasina intended to return to Bangladesh on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations, he said, "Desire and reality are two different things.""The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition...She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," Kobir said.Earlier, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali had told Reuters that the former prime minister intended to travel from Delhi to Dhaka on December 16 aboard Bangladesh's national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines.In an official communication, Ali said Hasina had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration for her return journey. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters.Meanwhile, Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) chief prosecutor Md Aminul Islam reportedly dismissed Hasina's demand for a state aircraft to facilitate her return, describing it as "nothing but madness".A Bangladeshi minister had also told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would face immediate arrest and imprisonment if she returned to the country. The minister added that no formal discussions had taken place with India over arranging an aircraft for her journey.Hasina served as Bangladesh's prime minister from 2009 until 2024. She fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a student-led agitation over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her Awami League government.She was subsequently sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal in a case involving crimes against humanity over the crackdown on protesters. Hasina has denied the allegations.Hasina first expressed her intention to return to Bangladesh during a virtual media briefing in August this year and reiterated the plan in several subsequent interviews.Earlier this month, she also applied for a fresh passport and national identity card through her legal representatives in the United Kingdom.Dhaka has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that the request is under examination.
Article Summary: West Bengal minister vows to avenge killings of Hindus in neighbouring Bangladesh. His remarks come amid heightened tensions in Bangladesh over the proposed return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India. Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kobir has said that Hasina would only be allowed to return as a "prisoner, in handcuffs" and under strict surveillance.

Article Title: 300 BJP, Hindu outfit members booked over Thiruparankundram Deepam protests
Article Text:
Deepathoon lamp row: Protests spread across Tamil Nadu, 300 booked in Madurai

NEW DELHI: Cases have been registered against around 300 members of the BJP and Hindu organisations for protesting in Tamil Nadu 's Thiruparankundram on Tuesday over the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop the hill, news agency ANI cited Madurai Police on Wednesday.According to the police, cases have been registered under six sections, including unlawful assembly without permission, causing a breach of public peace, making controversial remarks and obstructing government servants from discharging their duties.The protests were held over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court 's interim order directing that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the stone pillar.The Maha Deepam was instead lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills as part of the annual festival, amid heavy security and rising tensions. No lamp was lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar.A small team of priests associated with the Subramaniya Swamy Temple performed the lamp-lighting ceremony, while police personnel were deployed near the Deepathoon ahead of the scheduled time. The Supreme Court had directed that the lamp be lit at 6pm.Advocate and Hindu Munnani petitioner Niranjan S Kumar expressed disappointment over the decision and accused the state government of deliberately disobeying the Supreme Court's interim order."We were all in the belief that the government would take immediate steps to light the lamp at the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon. We had all gathered here to see the lamp being lit by the authorities themselves. Unfortunately, at 6:02 p.m., the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar was lit as usual, which means the order of the Supreme Court was definitely violated," he said.Alleging deliberate non-compliance with the court's directions, he added, "I would say it was not only violated, but it is a deliberate, calculated and willful disobedience of the order of the Supreme Court. So we are all left with no other option but to approach the Supreme Court by way of contempt."Niranjan also referred to the Supreme Court's direction to the Madurai District Collector to submit a status report within three days of the festival. He said further action would depend on the report."And the District Collector, Madurai, was also directed to file a status report within three days after the festival. So let's wait for the District Collector's report," he said.Tamil Nadu BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the state government's handling of the issue, accusing it of violating the Supreme Court's interim order and treating political groups differently."I strongly condemn the TVK government for violating the Supreme Court's interim order. Nobody is above the law. But they behaved in a way; they have violated the interim order of the Supreme Court," she said.Soundararajan questioned the decision to light the lamp at the Uchi Pillayar temple and accused the government of not informing people about the arrangements in advance."They are now citing the Agama rules; they have lit the lamp in the Uchi Pillayar. Till now, why didn't you say that you are cheating the people and you did not disclose where you are going to light the lamp? Beforehand you should have disclosed," she said.She also alleged that BJP leaders and workers were prevented from going near the temple, while leaders of some other political parties were allowed access."You did not allow us to go near the temple. The government did not allow us to go near the temple. From our State president to our workers, they were all arrested. We were not allowed to go to the temple. But they allowed Thirumavalavan; they allowed Jawahirullah," she said.Meanwhile, protests over the issue were reported from several other parts of Tamil Nadu.In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front staged a protest against the state government, alleging that it had failed to implement the Supreme Court's order. Police detained protesters who took part in a road blockade.In Pollachi, members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade during the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival, demanding that the state government follow the court's directions. Police removed the protesters and arrested them after they raised slogans against the government, triggering brief tension in the area.The protests came amid growing tensions over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar, with Hindu organisations demanding that the state government comply with the Supreme Court's interim directions.
Article Summary: Cases have been registered against around 300 members of the BJP and Hindu organisations. The protests were held over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon. The Maha Deepam was instead lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills.

Article Title: Anant Ambani’s Vantara signs 10-year wildlife conservation pact with Madagascar
Article Text:

Anant Ambani’s animal welfare and conservation organisation Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development to strengthen wildlife conservation and animal welfare efforts in the island nation.The non-exclusive Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed on November 24, 2026, recognises Vantara as Madagascar's conservation partner. The partnership will focus on returning Malagasy animals seized abroad, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, veterinary care, and rewilding, wherever possible.As part of the agreement, Vantara will support the development of Madagascar’s National Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre, expected to serve as a hub for conservation, research, and training. The facility will remain the property of the Republic of Madagascar and operate under the authority of its environment ministry.The collaboration will also focus on strengthening local expertise through training programmes, internships, specialist exchanges and applied research. Vantara may assist with health checks, disease screening, transportation, quarantine, and post-arrival care for animals being repatriated to Madagascar.The agreement comes amid growing concerns over the country's biodiversity. According to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, 90% of lemur species, which are endemic to Madagascar, are threatened with extinction, with nearly a third classified as Critically Endangered. The country has also faced challenges linked to illegal wildlife trade and habitat loss.Under the partnership, Vantara will provide scientific support, including field research and genetic profiling, to help determine whether rescued animals can be returned to the wild and to identify suitable release locations. The Government of Madagascar, guided by its CITES Scientific Authority.Madagascar's Environment and Sustainable Development Minister, Nolave Luck Aristide Andriatsihala, said international cooperation was essential to protecting the country's natural heritage.Vivaan Karani, CEO of Vantara, said strengthening the people and institutions responsible for wildlife conservation in animals' countries of origin would remain central to the organisation's conservation strategy.
Article Summary: Anant Ambani’s animal welfare and conservation organisation Vantara has signed a 10-year agreement with Madagascar. The partnership will focus on returning Malagasy animals seized abroad, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, veterinary care, and rewilding. The agreement comes amid growing concerns over the country's biodiversity.

Article Title: 'Customary practices, age-old traditions': Thiruparankundram temple clarifies why deepam was lit at usual spot
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple on Tuesday issued a clarification after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the 'Deepathoon', despite the Supreme Court 's order.In a statement, the temple's deputy commissioner and executive officer said that the Deepam is traditionally lit at the Deepa Mandapam located near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill."Specifically, as per the long-standing customary practice of the temple, the Karthigai Maha Deepam is traditionally lit at the Deepa Mandapam located near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill, directly above the sanctum of the presiding deity (Moolavar)," the statement read."Such long-standing and continuous religious practices (age-old continued practices), along with customs and rituals and Agama rules, are considered distinctive religious traditions and integral aspects of the temple's identity," it added.The statement said that the temple's board of trustees had unanimously passed a resolution stating that its age-old traditions and customary practices must be protected."Therefore, the temple's board of trustees has unanimously passed a resolution stating that the age-old traditions, customary practices, Agama regulations and established religious practices followed at the temple must be protected. Based on historical records establishing the continuity and religious significance of these practices, Agama-related documents and the opinions of temple functionaries (Sthanikars), the Board resolved to light the Karthigai Maha Deepam this year as well at the customary location," the statement read."It also resolved that the temple's traditions and customary practices should be brought to the attention of the court," it added."In accordance with the above resolution passed by the Board of Trustees, the Karthigai Maha Deepam of the temple was lit today, November 24, 2026, at around 6.00 pm, at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple atop the hill, directly above the sanctum of the presiding deity (Moolavar)," it added.This comes after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and police officials at Thiruparankundram after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the ‘Deepathoon’, despite the Supreme Court's order.Tamil Nadu law minister R Nirmal Kumar said in a brief statement that the Deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, close to the Uchipillaiyar Temple, which is right above the shrine of the presiding deity, Lord Subramania Swamy.The ceremony was held amid heightened security, with police detaining several people citing apprehensions of disorder based on intelligence inputs and their past conduct.The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill.Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.
Article Summary: Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple on Tuesday issued a clarification after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the 'Deepathoon' This comes after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and police officials. The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon.

Article Title: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
Article Text:
Mehbooba Mufti protests against deployment of heavy machinery along Amarnath Yatra route

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR/JAMMU: Amid the row over BRO’s construction work near the 11,780-foot-high Sheshnag Lake in Jammu & Kashmir, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti Tuesday attempted to trek to the spot but was stopped by police at Chandanwari, some 12 kms from the site.“My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder. What is being concealed today could become a man-made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath cave, yatra route and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole,” Mehbooba said.After a video of an earthmover purportedly near Sheshnag began circulating, the BRO (Border Roads Organisation) had clarified it was only carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety and environmental norms and its primary objective was to safeguard pilgrims throughout the yatra.MLA Hasnian Masoodi of the governing National Conference, however, rejected the BRO’s response. “If the track is being made safer, why are earthmovers being taken over there? This shouldn’t happen,” he added.Environmental activists say Sheshnag is a glacial lake and an ecologically fragile zone surrounded by steep slopes and glacial deposits. The lake is the source of the Lidder river, which flows downstream to Pahalgam and beyond into the Kashmir Valley.Sheshnag is among 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified in Jammu & Kashmir.Environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat warned that constructing a road around the Sheshnag glacier would be an environmental disaster. “More and more people must approach the Supreme Court, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) or the high court,” he said.On Monday, Congress MP and spokesperson Pawan Khera had said Sheshnag was not a construction site but a fragile Himalayan ecosystem and a sacred lake for both Hindus and Muslims.Meanwhile, BJP has defended the project, accusing Kashmir-based political parties and the Congress of communalising the issue.State BJP spokesperson Girdhari Lal Raina said certain political elements seem to have found a new pretext to communalise the atmosphere in the Amarnath Yatra track-widening issue. He said the BRO has clarified that the work concerns widening and stabilisation of vulnerable stretches of the existing Chandanwari-Amarnath track to ease congestion and improve pilgrim safety.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti attempts to trek to Sheshnag Lake in Jammu & Kashmir. PDP chief stopped by police at Chandanwari, some 12 kms from the site. Environmental activists warn that constructing a road around the glacier would be an environmental disaster.

Article Title: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
Article Text:
NSA Ajit Doval met Maldives' minister of defence and national service Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the eighth Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) NSA-level meeting

NEW DELHI: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval called on Maldives defence minister Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting and discussed ways to strengthen defence and security cooperation between the two countries.This was the first high-level contact between the two countries after President Mohamed Muizzu's visit to Pakistan recently. That visit raised eyebrows here as Maldives signed 20 MoUs with Pakistan, including in areas like defence and maritime cooperation. Muizzu had also called for the resumption of the Saarc summit process during his visit.Doval is in Male for the CSC, which was formed to promote closer cooperation between member states on vital matters of security and to strengthen partnerships for enhancing regional security in the Indian Ocean Region.Originally launched in 2011 as a trilateral maritime security dialogue involving India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, the grouping later inducted Mauritius, Bangladesh, and Seychelles into its fold.
Article Summary: National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval called on Maldives defence minister Hassan Rasheed on the sidelines of the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting. This was the first high-level contact between the two countries after President Mohamed Muizzu's visit to Pakistan recently.

At least 13 people were killed and 14 injured after a bus collided with a truck in the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah on Tuesday. Indian nationals were among those killed, the Indian consulate in Dubai confirmed.The bus was carrying 41 passengers when it crashed into a truck parked on the roadside following a technical breakdown, according to local authorities. The accident took place on Al Watan Road in the early hours of Tuesday. Rescue teams rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to nearby hospitals.The death toll initially stood at 11 but rose to 13 after two injured passengers died in hospital. It said further details were being ascertained.

Article Title: Karthigai Deepam row: Why lighting a lamp has triggered a legal battle in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Karthigai deepam row (PTI image)

What is the Karthigai Deepam row?

What did the Supreme Court order on November 20

What happened on November 24

Why did the Madurai collector say the lamp could not be lit at Deepathoon

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government apologised before the Supreme Court on Wednesday after the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp was not lit at the designated Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 24, despite the court's interim direction.In a status report filed by Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna, the state government said the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to carry out the ritual and instead decided to retain the customary location.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, which was the subject of the Supreme Court's November 20 order. The court said it would consider the contempt plea alleging non-compliance with its directions and asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications.The dispute over the ritual's location has been continuing for years, with Hindu groups seeking permission to light the lamp at the hilltop stone pillar near the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, while the state government and temple authorities have maintained that the customary venue is near the Ucchi Pillayar temple.Also read| ‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in Supreme Court, contempt plea to be heard in Karthigai Deepam row The November 24 ceremony, the subsequent explanation by the district administration and the demand for contempt proceedings have now brought the dispute back before the Supreme Court.Karthigai Deepam is a traditional Tamil Hindu festival celebrated by lighting lamps in homes and temples. At Thiruparankundram, the dispute concerns the location where the ceremonial lamp, or Maha Deepam, should be lit during the annual festival.For decades, the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of Thiruparankundram hill. However, Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.The disagreement is not limited to the ritual's location. It also involves competing claims over the stone pillar's character and the hilltop's ownership and status. While Hindu groups describe Deepathoon as an ancient structure associated with the ritual, another side argues that it is a survey stone. The dargah committee has also contested the demand, claiming ownership of the hilltop.The dispute has travelled through the courts over several years. In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at Deepathoon. A division bench upheld the direction in its January 6, 2026, judgment. The state government subsequently challenged the High Court's decision before the Supreme Court.The Tamil Nadu government and the temple administration have maintained that the lamp has traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple. The state has also raised concerns over the legal and administrative implications of allowing the ritual at the disputed pillar, including the possibility of law-and-order complications because of its proximity to the dargah.On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. The order came while the Supreme Court was hearing challenges to the Madras High Court's directions on the ritual.The court allowed only a restricted team authorised by the temple administration and government officials to go to the location and carry out the ceremony. It also designated the district collector as the nodal officer responsible for coordination and supervision.The Supreme Court imposed safeguards to prevent any escalation at the disputed site. It restrained members of the public from going to the location and prohibited processions, public gatherings, slogan-raising and demonstrations during the ceremony. The court also stayed portions of the Madras High Court judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at Deepathoon.Importantly, the permission was limited to November 24 and did not settle the larger dispute over the ritual's history, the hilltop's ownership, or any customary or religious right to light the lamp at the pillar. The court clarified that neither the permission nor the ceremony could be treated as proof of an established custom or a continuing right of access to the location.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently approached the Supreme Court seeking a review of the November 20 order and a stay on the one-time permission. However, the interim direction remained the basis for the November 24 arrangements.The Karthigai Deepam ceremony took place amid heightened security and tension at Thiruparankundram on November 24. However, the lamp was not lit at Deepathoon, the location specified by the Supreme Court. Instead, the Maha Deepam was lit at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple at around 6 pm.The development came hours after Madurai collector Nishant Krishna told the Madurai bench of the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's directions would be implemented. The High Court had also reminded officials of their responsibility to comply with the apex court's order and warned of contempt proceedings in the event of non-compliance.State law minister C T R Nirmalkumar confirmed the lighting at the customary location in a post on X, saying: "Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near Ucchi Pillaiyar temple, directly above the sanctum sanctorum of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram".The decision triggered protests by Hindu organisations and BJP workers, who demanded that the government implement the Supreme Court's direction. Tensions were reported near the hill, where protesters raised slogans against the state government. Police had deployed more than 5,600 personnel in Thiruparankundram and adjoining areas, with restrictions imposed on public access to the hilltop.The district administration later said that the last-minute decision to retain the customary venue followed concerns raised by the temple's Board of Trustees. The trustees maintained that the Deepa Mandapam was the traditional location for the ritual and that the practice should continue there.In a status report filed before the Supreme Court, Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna said the administration had made arrangements to implement the November 20 order but could not proceed because the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the team proposed to light the lamp.According to the district administration's explanation, the Supreme Court had designated the collector as the coordinating officer, while the temple administration was responsible for authorising the personnel who would carry out the ritual. The administration said it had completed the necessary arrangements, but the trustees eventually resolved to retain the customary location.The Board of Trustees cited religious traditions and established worship practices in support of its decision. It maintained that the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple was the customary venue and that the location was directly above the head of Lord Murugan, the presiding deity. The trustees also referred to Agama rules governing temple rituals and festivals.In its statement after the ceremony, the district administration said: "The trustees unanimously resolved to retain the customary venue, citing religious traditions and established worship practices."The trustees said their decision followed an examination of historical and religious records and consultations with the temple's Sthanikars, or hereditary ritual functionaries. They also decided to place their findings before the court.The collector apologised for the failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon and maintained that the administration had made every effort to comply with the Supreme Court's direction. The state's position was that the district administration could not independently authorise another team to perform the ritual in the absence of the temple Board of Trustees' approval.The status report also maintained that there had been no wilful or deliberate disobedience of the Supreme Court's directions. The government said the failure to carry out the ceremony at the designated location was due to the trustees' decision to retain the customary venue.The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon led to demands for contempt proceedings against the state authorities. The petitioner seeking permission for the ritual alleged that the government had failed to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 direction despite assurances given before the Madras High Court that the order would be implemented.During Wednesday's proceedings, a senior advocate appearing for the petitioner termed the developments "most unfortunate". He argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there, and alleged deliberate non-compliance with the apex court's directions.The counsel also urged the Supreme Court to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned. When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt plea, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see."The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications and said it would hear the matter. The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi also said it would peruse the status report filed by the state government.The contempt allegation centres on whether the authorities failed to implement the Supreme Court's specific direction despite the district administration being tasked with coordinating the ceremony. The state government, however, has denied wilful disobedience and attributed the failure to the temple trustees' decision not to authorise the proposed team.The Supreme Court's consideration of the contempt plea will therefore bring the conduct of the officials and the explanation submitted by the district administration under judicial scrutiny.The failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon has triggered sharp criticism from BJP leaders, who have accused the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government of disregarding the Supreme Court's interim order and hurting the sentiments of devotees.BJP national general secretary B L Santhosh accused the state government of defying the court's directions and said the government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge". In a post on X, he alleged that the Madurai district administration had lit the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar Mandapam instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar as directed by the Supreme Court.Also read| ‘Crores of devotees let down’: BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row In another post, Santhosh accused the government of compromising the sentiments of devotees to accommodate its political allies. He said: "You people have hurt devotes & defied SC Order to please some alliance partners & you yourself is Law Minister of a Govt which will fully defied SC Order . To please some friends you let down crores of devotees," he alleged.Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran also accused the state government and district administration of failing to implement the court's order. He criticised the decision to light the lamp at the customary location after the collector had assured the Madras High Court that the Supreme Court's direction would be followed."Lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made is an act of deception. It is akin to fooling a child with candy, and they are attempting to deceive the Supreme Court and High Court judges," Nagenthran said.BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also accused the government of violating the interim order and alleged that the decision was taken to appease its alliance partners. She questioned why the government had not raised its objections based on Agama rules before the Supreme Court.The BJP's criticism came alongside protests by Hindu organisations in different parts of Tamil Nadu. Demonstrations were reported in Ramanathapuram and Pollachi, where protesters demanded that the government comply with the Supreme Court's direction. Police detained protesters involved in road blockades, while cases were registered against members of BJP and Hindu organisations over the demonstrations.The state government and temple trustees, however, have defended the decision to retain the customary location, citing religious traditions and established worship practices.
Article Summary: Karthigai Deepam is a traditional Tamil Hindu festival celebrated by lighting lamps in homes and temples. At Thiruparankundram, the dispute concerns the location where the ceremonial lamp, or Maha Deepam, should be lit during the annual festival. Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar located higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. The dispute has travelled through the courts over several years.

NEW DELHI: A court on Wednesday sentenced three BJP-RSS workers to life imprisonment for the 2016 murder of CPM activist CV Dhanaraj in Kannur district.The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh on each of the convicts.Taliparamba Additional Sessions Judge KN Prashanth had found TP Biju (34), M Vipin (34) and M Vaishakh (31), who are brothers, guilty of the murder on November 23. The court acquitted 16 other accused in the case.The three convicts were sentenced to life imprisonment under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court directed that the total fine of Rs 15 lakh be paid to Dhanaraj's family, particularly his wife and mother.They were also awarded a total of five years and four months of imprisonment each under various other IPC sections, including Sections 447, 323 and 506(II).Special Public Prosecutor CK Sreedharan said the life sentences would begin after the convicts complete their prison terms. They would also face additional imprisonment if they fail to pay the fines.Speaking to reporters, Sreedharan said the prosecution was satisfied with the quantum of punishment but would challenge the acquittal of the 16 accused, particularly those allegedly involved in the conspiracy.The court did not consider the case to fall under the 'rarest of rare' category that warrants the death penalty. However, it observed that the murder was a planned and deliberate act, even though the prosecution failed to establish the charge of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the IPC.Sreedharan said the prosecution had presented evidence against certain individuals allegedly involved in the conspiracy and would study the 147-page judgment before deciding on further legal action.The court also directed the District Legal Services Authority to assess the financial condition of Dhanaraj's family and consider providing them additional assistance.What happened in the 2016 murderDhanaraj, the CPM branch secretary at Ezhimala, was hacked to death on July 11, 2016, while returning home at Ramanthali near Payyannur.According to the prosecution, a group of assailants followed him on motorcycles and attacked him with sharp weapons near his house. He was hacked and stabbed to death in front of his mother and wife.A total of 20 BJP-RSS workers were named as accused in the case. However, the trial was completed against only 19, as the 12th accused, C Biju, also known as Churakkattu Biju, was later murdered.The trial began on September 25, 2025. The court examined 43 witnesses, while the prosecution produced 177 documents and 33 material exhibits.The case was initially investigated by V Ramesan, the then Payyannur Circle Inspector. The investigation was later completed by MP Asad, who filed the chargesheet.The murder case had recently returned to the political spotlight after former CPM district committee member V Kunhikrishnan alleged irregularities in the collection of funds raised in the name of Dhanaraj's martyrdom.Kunhikrishnan was subsequently expelled from the party and later won the Payyannur Assembly seat as an independent candidate backed by the Congress-led UDF.
Article Summary: Court sentences three BJP-RSS workers to life imprisonment for the 2016 murder of CPM activist CV Dhanaraj. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh on each of the convicts. TP Biju (34), M Vipin (34) and M Vaishakh (31), who are brothers, were found guilty of the murder on November 23.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London over alleged discrepancies in his passport details, particularly his place of birth.Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union on December 1. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.The development followed a show-cause notice issued to Das by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, on Monday evening, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his birth-related documents within seven days. The notice warned that his passport could be impounded under the Passports Act, 1967, if he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation.According to government sources, inconsistencies in details such as his date of birth and father's name were flagged across documents, including his Aadhaar card, passport and school certificate. The authorities initiated a fresh verification of his documents and information recorded in his passport application.The passport was originally issued to Das on August 21, 2019, following the verification process.According to government officials, a passport holder issued a show-cause notice over allegedly incorrect particulars cannot use the passport for international travel until the matter is resolved.An official told TOI, "As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of."Another government officer said Das had time until November 30 to respond to the notice. The official added that he could resume international travel using the same passport once the RPO completed its re-verification and cleared the documents.However, Das said he became aware of the notice only after reaching the airport, claiming that it had been issued just hours before his scheduled departure.Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Das questioned the timing of the notice and the discrepancies flagged by the authorities, pointing out that his passport had been issued in 2019 after police verification and that he had undertaken several international trips since then.“How was I issued the passport which was given after police verification?” he asked.Alleging that the action was linked to his association with the CJP, Das said, “I was scheduled to talk in various prestigious universities in London on their invitation. That trip couldn’t be completed because the coward govt has flagged my passport citing some discrepancies...”Apart from the Oxford Union panel discussion, Das said he was scheduled to participate in engagements involving Cambridge University, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh.The Oxford Union event was scheduled for December 1, with Das and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke listed as key panellists on the organisation's website.Explaining the purpose of his proposed engagements, Das said he intended to discuss the growth of the CJP movement and its use of non-violent methods.“The Indian students studying there wanted to understand what CJP movement is and how it grew. I would have spoken about how this movement without violence could become successful. How the world’s Gen Z could learn from us,” he said.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh, who was also scheduled to travel to the UK, said her visa had been rejected a few days earlier. Dipke said he had also received an invitation but was scheduled to attend a CJP programme in Nagpur on November 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.The London School of Economics Students' Union Amnesty International Society subsequently announced that its event featuring Das had been indefinitely postponed. In a statement, it condemned what it described as an “arbitrary obstruction” and the “apparent targeting of an individual seeking to engage in academic dialogue and public discussion”.The society expressed solidarity with Das and said it would share updates if the event could be rescheduled.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the decision to stop Das from travelling, drawing comparisons with the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi.“Is he (Das) a terrorist, a criminal? Why was he stopped?” Dipke asked at a separate press conference.Meanwhile, a public interest litigation has also been filed in the Madras High Court concerning alleged inconsistencies in Das's birth and parentage documents, while also questioning his citizenship.The passport authorities' re-verification process is pending, with Das required to respond to the show-cause notice by November 30.
Article Summary: CJP co-convener Saurav Das moved the Delhi high court after immigration authorities stopped him from boarding a flight to London. Das was scheduled to travel to the United Kingdom for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by the Oxford Union. His passport was flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday, preventing him from travelling.

Article Title: ‘Crores of devotees let down’: BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row

NEW DELHI: The controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram hills escalated on Wednesday, with BJP national general secretary BL Santhosh accusing the TVK-led government of defying the Supreme Court 's interim order and warning that Chief Minister Vijay's government would face a "civilisational and legal challenge".The remarks came after the traditional lamp was lit at the Ucchi Pillayar temple on Tuesday evening instead of the Deepathoon stone pillar, as directed by the Supreme Court. The apex court had ordered that the lamp be lit at the designated pillar at 6 pm, triggering a dispute between the state administration and organisations demanding implementation of the direction.In a post on X, Santhosh alleged that the Madurai district administration had violated the court's directions."The DM of Madurai who is a part of TN government, defies SC order and lights Karthika Deepam at Ucchapillaiyar Mandapam instead of Deepathoon Stone pillar as instructed by SC," he said.Targeting the government led by Vijay, he added, "@TVKVijayHQ Govt under @actorvijay will face both civilisational & legal challenge. They have bit more than they can chew."In another post, Santhosh accused the government of compromising the sentiments of devotees to accommodate its political allies."You people have hurt devotes & defied SC Order to please some alliance partners & you yourself is Law Minister of a Govt which will fully defied SC Order . To please some friends you let down crores of devotees," he alleged.The BJP leader's remarks came amid protests by Hindu organisations and BJP workers across Tamil Nadu over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon pillar.Several organisations staged demonstrations in different parts of the state, demanding that the government implement the Supreme Court's directions.In Ramanathapuram, members of the Hindu Front organised a protest against the state government, accusing it of failing to comply with the court order. Police detained protesters involved in a road blockade in the Kenikarai area.In Pollachi, members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade during the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival. Protesters alleged that Hindu organisations, including the BJP and Vishva Hindu Parishad, had been campaigning since last year for the lamp to be lit at the designated pillar.The demonstrators raised slogans against the state government and demanded that it follow the court's directions within the stipulated time. Police personnel deployed at the site removed the protesters and arrested them.Advocate Niranjan S Kumar, who is associated with the Hindu Munnani petition in the matter, expressed disappointment over the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon and accused the state government of deliberately disobeying the Supreme Court's interim order."We were all in the belief that the government would take immediate steps to light the lamp at the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon. We had all gathered here to see the lamp being lit by the authorities themselves. Unfortunately, at 6:02 p.m., the lamp at the Ucchi Pillayar was lit as usual, which means the order of the Supreme Court was definitely violated. I would say it was not only violated, but it is a deliberate, calculated and willful disobedience of the order of the Supreme Court. So we are all left with no other option but to approach the Supreme Court by way of contempt. I trust and hope that the Supreme Court will take note of all these actions and see that it passes serious action against the state," the advocate said.He also referred to the Supreme Court's direction asking the Madurai District Collector to submit a status report within three days after the festival."And the District Collector, Madurai, was also directed to file a status report within three days after the festival. So let's wait for the District Collector's report. In my personal view, I would say this is nothing but a constitutional breakdown. The machinery has been broken down and the State has deliberately violated the interim order of the Supreme Court. Therefore, this is nothing but a constitutional breakdown of the machinery. The Supreme Court has to take note of all these things and pass, and we expect that it will deal with this with iron hands..."Tamil Nadu BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the Vijay government, accusing it of violating the Supreme Court's interim order and discriminating against political groups in its handling of the temple dispute."I strongly condemn the TVK government for violating the Supreme Court's interim order. Nobody is above the law. But they behaved in a way; they have violated the interim order of the Supreme Court. They should not have gone for an appeal; that is my view. They are now citing because of the Agama rules, they have lit the lamp in the Ucchi Pillayar. Till now, why didn't you say that you are cheating the people and you did not disclose where you are going to light the lamp? Before itself you should have disclosed. Why didn't you put the same argument before the Supreme Court? They did not tell about the Agama rules at that time. Madras High Court again said - don't cheat like the previous time because it cannot be excused repeatedly."She alleged that the government had taken the decision to appease its alliance partners and claimed that BJP leaders and workers were prevented from approaching the temple."I am saying only one thing to the TVK government, to CM Vijay - to pamper your alliance partners, to satisfy your alliance partners, you have taken this decision. But these alliance partners were the alliance partners of the previous government, they backstabbed them and now they have joined with you. They will definitely backstab you. You did not allow us to go near the temple. The government did not allow us to go near the temple. From our State president to our workers, they were all arrested. We were not allowed to go to the temple. But they allowed Thirumavalavan, they allowed Jawahirullah. Jawahirullah is a person with different religious beliefs. How can he talk about the religious ideology of the Hindu faith? TVK government is not treating us equally."Soundararajan further called on the Supreme Court to take note of the alleged violation."It is atrocious, disheartening and they have disobeyed the rule of law. Supreme Court should definitely consider this violation and in future, the TVK government will pay a high price for this. You can cheat the Supreme Court, you can violate the High Court but you cannot cheat the people's court. People will answer you. Because the same people answered DMK and sent them home because of the anti-Hindu attitude."Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran also accused the state government and Madurai district administration of failing to implement the Supreme Court's directions.Speaking to reporters in Tirunelveli on Tuesday, Nagenthran said the authorities had failed to light the lamp at the Deepathoon despite the apex court's directions and subsequent intervention by the Madras High Court.He alleged that lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made amounted to deceiving the judiciary."Lighting the lamp at the Pillaiyar temple after assuring the court that arrangements were being made is an act of deception. It is akin to fooling a child with candy, and they are attempting to deceive the Supreme Court and High Court judges," Nagenthran said.He argued that the Madurai District Collector, as district magistrate, had the authority to implement court orders independently and should not yield to political pressure. He also said the collector should be considered the "first accused" in the matter.The BJP leader said the party would decide on further legal action based on the observations of the Supreme Court.The Maha Deepam was lit above the Ucchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram hills on Tuesday evening amid heavy police deployment and heightened tensions. However, the lamp was not lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar, which was at the centre of the legal dispute.A small team of priests associated with the Subramaniya Swamy Temple performed the lighting ceremony at the Ucchi Pillayar location, while police personnel remained deployed near the Deepathoon pillar.The Supreme Court had issued an interim direction for lighting the lamp at the designated pillar at 6 pm. The Madurai District Collector was also asked to submit a status report within three days after the festival.The dispute has since triggered protests, political allegations and demands for further judicial intervention.
Article Summary: BJP national general secretary BL Santhosh accuses TVK-led government of defying the Supreme Court's interim order. He warns that Chief Minister Vijay's government will face a "civilisational and legal challenge" Demonstrations held across Tamil Nadu over the failure to light the lamp at the Deepathoon pillar.

He also took a swipe at the party's rivals, saying SP supporters were "grounded" and did not think beyond the cycle, unlike those who aspired for cars, helicopters and planes.Asked whether he had any doubts or fears, the SP leader claimed that people were staying silent out of fear."If the ruler is cruel, people will be afraid. It is because of this fear that people are silent. BJP accuses critics of politicising issue

NEW DELHI: A video showing a JCB operating near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route in Jammu and Kashmir has triggered a political row, with leaders and environmentalists questioning the construction activity in the fragile glacial zone.The controversy has intensified after political leaders raised concerns over the environmental impact and religious significance of the landscape, while an online petition seeking a halt to construction near Kashmir's alpine lakes gained traction.The Border Roads Organisation (BRO), however, said post-Amarnath Yatra works were being carried out in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.A video showing an excavator operating near Sheshnag Lake, a high-altitude glacial lake in south Kashmir's Anantnag district, has drawn criticism from political parties, religious leaders and environmentalists, who have demanded that the activity be stopped.The deployment of heavy machinery near the lake has raised concerns about potential ecological damage to the fragile alpine landscape along the Amarnath cave route.The controversy has also brought the area's religious significance into focus, with leaders questioning whether construction activity could affect the landscape associated with the annual pilgrimage.The BRO on Monday said post-Amarnath Yatra works were being carried out in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.PDP president Mehbooba Mufti expressed alarm over reports of excavation near Sheshnag, saying the use of heavy machinery in the ecologically fragile zone could threaten both the environment and the pilgrimage's religious sanctity.Mehbooba, accompanied by party MLAs Waheed Para and Syed Muntazir Mehndi, set out towards Sheshnag on Tuesday morning along the Amarnath Yatra route. The PDP leaders attempted to trek from Chandanwari towards Sheshnag but were stopped by police.The former chief minister said forests, mountains and glaciers, including Sheshnag, play a role in the formation of the naturally occurring ice lingam at the Amarnath cave during the pilgrimage."My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder. What is being concealed today could become a man made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath Cave, Yatra and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole," she said in a post on X.JKPDP spokesperson Mohit Bhan also criticised the construction activity, pointing to the religious significance of Sheshnag and the need to protect its ecological surroundings."We have seen Joshimath, Kedarnath, Mata Vaishno Devi, and the devastation caused by cloudbursts in the Amarnath region. Yet, we refuse to learn. Sacred destinations are being reduced to commercial and picnic spots at the cost of fragile ecosystems. The conversation must go beyond Amarnath and Sheshnag. Shrinking Dal and Wular, rampant encroachments, conversion of agricultural land and felling of mighty Chinars are all part of the same crisis. Our forefathers protected this shared natural and spiritual inheritance for centuries. We must reclaim that responsibility. Heads must roll, accountability must follow and preservation must take precedence over reckless development," Bhan.Kashmir's chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, also raised concerns over the activity and urged people to oppose what he described as ecological destruction in fragile areas."We all have to collectively raise our voice to stop the mindless destruction of our ecology at its most fragile places," he said.Mirwaiz questioned chief minister Omar Abdullah's silence on the issue and urged authorities to intervene. He also cited retreating glaciers and recent glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal to underline the vulnerability of the Himalayan region."With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such 'developmental projects'," he said on X.He emphasised that mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection, "not plunder", for present and future generations. "So this must be immediately stopped," he said.Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra questioned the deployment of a JCB excavator near Sheshnag Lake and sought clarity on the purpose of the work and the permissions granted by various departments."I was surprised to see how the JCB reached Sheshnag. From what we could make out in the video, it appeared to be digging soil and dumping it on the left-hand side, towards the lake," PTI quoted Karra as saying.He said reports suggesting that the agency concerned had obtained no-objection certificates (NOCs) from various departments made it important to establish the purpose of the activity."But for which project was it taken there? Which department is involved? Which department granted the NOC, and which other departments gave their approval? It is very important to obtain information about this," he said.The Congress leader urged the government to clarify its position and make details of the project and approvals public.An online petition on Change.org titled "Stop construction around Kashmir's alpine lakes", started by Zarqua Banday, has garnered nearly 1,600 signatures so far. It calls for a halt to construction activity near ecologically fragile alpine lakes and urges authorities to engage with environmental and community groups to develop a sustainable way forward.The petition argues that road construction in untouched areas could damage fragile ecosystems and increase pollution, habitat destruction and tourist pressure."This isn't progress; it's a threat to our environment," it said.The petition also called for sustainable tourism initiatives, including guided trekking, limited access permits and eco-friendly accommodation, instead of road construction in fragile areas.It cited the Swiss Alps as an example of regions that have adopted strategies to manage tourism while protecting the environment.The petition said people in Kashmir are not opposed to development but want it to respect the region's land, traditions and ecological balance.The Jammu and Kashmir BJP on Tuesday accused critics of selective environmental activism and double standards, saying it would oppose attempts to communalise development, undermine the Amarnath pilgrimage or disturb peace in the Valley.J&K BJP spokesperson and former MLC Girdhari Lal Raina said the controversy was being used for political purposes."What is being projected as an environmental issue increasingly appears to be an attempt to manufacture controversy, disturb the peaceful atmosphere and exploit religious sentiments for narrow political gains," he said.Without naming any party or individual, Raina accused political parties and leaders of attempting to revive the Amarnath land controversy and communalise the issue.
Article Summary: A video showing a JCB operating near Sheshnag Lake in Jammu and Kashmir has triggered a political row. Political leaders have raised concerns over the environmental impact and religious significance of the landscape. An online petition seeking a halt to construction near Kashmir's alpine lakes has gained traction.

NEW DELHI: The Congress, an ally of Tamil Nadu's ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), on Tuesday welcomed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at its traditional spot, instead of the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai.In an interim one-time order passed on November 20, the Supreme Court allowed the Karthigai Deepam to be lit at the Deepathoon, instead of its usual spot above the Uchhipillaiyar temple.On Monday, the Madras high court also directed authorities to comply with the top court's order."The lamp was lit at the place where it was supposed to be lit. ...
