Article Summary: The Congress welcomed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at its traditional spot, instead of the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai. The BJP criticised the TVK government, branding it "anti-Hindu" The ceremony took place amid tight security, with 5,618 police personnel deployed.

Article Title: Huang in there! Trump's bra-zen tribute to tech bro he rescued
Article Text:
Trump's red-bra meme celebrating Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia sparks backlash over presidential decorum, national security and double standards

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MAGA boss Donald Trump has never been one to let conventional presidential decorum get in the way of a provocative social-media stunt. So when Nvidia chief Jensen Huang returned to his corporate throne after an extra-marital affairs scandal, the US President, himself a seasoned veteran in this sphere, celebrated it by posting a meme of Huang waving a red bra in place of a clenched fist he (Trump) had raised after surviving an assassination attempt.Trump was apparently having a laugh, but not everyone was amused. On CNN, Scott Jennings, the conservative commentator and Trump defender, was challenged by guest host Elie Honig to explain the image. Told to lighten up and that it was just a joke, Honig reminded him of Cory Comperatore, the man who lost his life during the assassination attempt and asked, "Do you think his family is laughing?"For critics, the issue is not so much about Trump's bizarre sense of humour, but that the office of the presidency has become a social-media trolling operation. One angry reaction captured the sentiment with copulatory nouns and verbs, accusing Trump of having "degraded and debased the institution of the presidency" and lamenting a political culture in which billionaire interests seemed to matter more than public standards.Others questioned what message the President was sending about fidelity and accountability. Here was a man with his own long and well-documented history of marital infidelity and sex scandals, making light of another powerful man's extramarital relationships.The objection was not necessarily that Huang should be denied a second chance. It was the apparent double standard: personal conduct that might have serious consequences for ordinary employees or executives was being transformed into a badge of masculine resilience when the person involved was sufficiently powerful, wealthy or strategically useful.There was, meanwhile, another curious dimension to Trump's defence of Huang. Having pronounced him a patriot and a national asset, the president introduced an ethnic qualification that was distinctly less reassuring. Huang was born in Taiwan, and Trump suggested that, had Washington failed to bring him back, China might have recruited him to lead Huawei's AI operations. "He's got a little Chinese blood in him," Trump said, suggesting that if Huang had been treated badly, he might have been tempted by an offer from Beijing. It was an extraordinary observation, not least because it appeared to conflate ethnicity with national allegiance.The controversy also exposed a more consequential contradiction within Trump's own camp. Several Republican lawmakers have questioned both Huang's reinstatement and the administration's intervention. Senators including Tom Cotton and Pete Ricketts have insisted that the company's national-security questions remain unresolved and that Huang must still answer congressional inquiries. The concerns relate not simply to his personal relationships but to possible exposure of sensitive American semiconductor technology to China.Trump, however, has shown little inclination to follow the Republican establishment's preferred script. On China, as with Russia, he has resisted the hawkish instincts of his own party. On immigration, tariffs, foreign policy and even the conduct of the federal government, he has repeatedly departed from conventional Republican positions, often demanding that his party fall in line behind him.The question increasingly being asked is not simply what Trump will do next, but what, if anything, constitutes a red line for him and for the Republican Party that has largely accommodated his instincts. If a president can personally lobby for the reinstatement of a billionaire executive facing national-security questions, dismiss the surrounding scandal as potentially good publicity and then celebrate the outcome with a lingerie meme built around an assassination attempt, what exactly is beyond the pale?For Trump, perhaps nothing is. Every controversy is an opportunity, every outrage an audience, and every institutional convention another obstacle to be trampled, preferably with a camera rolling. The Huang affair is particularly revealing because Trump has managed to combine several presidential roles in a single episode: corporate dealmaker, national-security arbiter, moral relativist, ethnic commentator, and internet comedian. He has intervened in and influenced a private company's boardroom decision, vouched for an executive facing serious questions, and then turned the executive's sexual scandal into a piece of presidential entertainment. Even his most trenchant critics admit this: No one, absolutely no one, could have done this.
Article Summary: Donald Trump's red-bra meme celebrating Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia sparks backlash over presidential decorum, national security and double standards. The issue is not so much about Trump's bizarre sense of humour, but that the office of the presidency has become a social-media trolling operation. The controversy also exposed a more consequential contradiction within Trump's own camp.

Article Title: Israel govt formation: Eisenkot, Lieberman seal first coalition pact as rivals step up push to oust Netanyahu
Article Text:
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, attends his party's faction meeting at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, in Jerusalem, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Ohad Zwigenberg)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing opposition party on Tuesday, marking the first such alliance since last month's election.Yashar said Eisenkot met Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and the two agreed on a deal following their discussions, Reuters reported.Efforts to form a government without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are gathering pace.The Knesset was sworn in on November 10 without a new government in place, after the October 27 vote cost Netanyahu his majority but left his rivals without a clear route to power. President Isaac Herzog has asked Eisenkot to form a government, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.Eisenkot has until December 6 to assemble a government under his 28-day mandate, with the option of a 14-day extension. Should he fail, Netanyahu will get a chance to try, and if neither succeeds, Israel will go to another election next year, Reuters reported.Netanyahu's Likud alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties secured 53 of the 120 Knesset seats, short of a majority of 61. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar and its potential partners, Lieberman's party among them, hold 48.Arab parties, which have 19 seats and share Eisenkot's opposition to Netanyahu, could give his bloc a path to a majority.Yashar and Israel Our Home won 21 and seven seats, respectively. The deal comes despite Lieberman's earlier objections to a government reliant on Arab party support or to joining a unity government with Netanyahu. Lieberman has repeatedly said his main goal is to remove Netanyahu from power.Talks are also under way between Eisenkot, some members of the so-called change bloc and Likud on a possible unity government. Separately, the left-wing Democrats party, which holds eight seats, announced it was suspending negotiations with Eisenkot, citing his progress in talks with Likud and a stalemate in efforts to form a change government. Party leader Yair Golan has said he favours a government without Netanyahu that includes Arab parties.
Article Summary: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing opposition party on Tuesday. The deal comes despite Lieberman's earlier objections to a government reliant on Arab party support or to joining a unity government with Netanyahu.

Article Title: TN lights lamp away from site approved by SC
Article Text:
People at the Deepathoon (stone pillar) atop Thirupparankundram hillock; the ceremonial lamp lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchhi Pillayar temple

Temple trustees resolved to retain customary venue, says dist admin





MADURAI: Defying a Supreme Court order, the Vijay-led TVK govt in Tamil Nadu lit the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp Tuesday evening at the original spot near a hilltop shrine in Madurai, skipping the designated "deepathoon" pillar atop Thiruparankundram hillock.The 6pm ceremony took place hours after district collector Nishant Krishna assured Madras HC's Madurai bench that the state would abide by SC's Nov 20 order."Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit at Deepa Mandapam near Ucchi Pillaiyar temple, directly above the sanctum sanctorum of the presiding deity..." state law minister CTR Nirmalkumar wrote on X, sharing photos .SC had directed the lamp lighting at Deepathoon, near Sikandar Badusha dargah, as “a one-time measure”. Multiple groups have been locked in battle over lighting the lamp at Deepathoon, which some regard as an ancient structure while others call it “a survey stone”.An HC division bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi had warned district officials of contempt proceedings if the SC order wasn’t complied with.The administration later blamed the trustees for what happened. In a statement issued after the ceremony, the district administration said the last-minute departure from its decision to adhere to the apex court’s order was prompted by concerns raised by the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple.“The trustees unanimously resolved to retain the customary venue, citing religious traditions and established worship practices,” it said.The trustees defended the choice on the ground of Agama rules governing temple rituals and festivals. The Deepa Mandapam, they said, sits directly above the head of the presiding deity, Murugan, and has served as the venue for the ritual for generations. “The traditions and established practices of the temple must be preserved.”Board chairperson V Shanmugasundaram, deputy commissioner and executive officer G Selvi and four trustees said the resolution was adopted after examining historical and religious records and consulting the temple Sthanikars, the hereditary ritual functionaries.The board said it would place these findings before the court. The district administration, for its part, said it held detailed meetings and completed all arrangements before the trustees intervened. State BJP president Nainar Nagenthran accused CM C Joseph Vijay’s govt of tricking the judiciary. “They have deceived SC and high court judges, just as children are deceived by giving them chocolates,” he said.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santhosh said govt defied SC to appease its alliance partners, letting down crores of devotees. VCK president and MP Thol Thirumavalavan congratulated CM Vijay for “thwarting” what he called the “Sangh Parivar’s conspiracy”. He said the state had protected Tamil religious traditions and harmony despite political pressure.More than 5,600 police personnel were deployed in Thiruparankundram and adjoining areas of Madurai to prevent any flare-up. Prohibitory orders will remain in force across the district until 10am Wednesday. Last year, the DMK govt had ignored an HC order, allowing the same.
Article Summary: The Vijay-led TVK govt in Tamil Nadu lit the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp Tuesday evening at the original spot near a hilltop shrine in Madurai. Multiple groups have been locked in battle over lighting the lamp at Deepathoon, which some regard as an ancient structure while others call it “a survey stone”

Article Title: DU student found dead in Faridabad hotel, cops start murder probe despite suicide note
Article Text:
(Representative) A 19-year-old female student was discovered dead in a hotel room after leaving home for college





GURGAON: A 19-year-old Delhi University student, who left home telling her parents she was going to college, was found dead in a Faridabad hotel room the next morning.She had checked in with a neighbour, who allegedly left during the night. Though police found a bottle of rat poison and a handwritten note in the room, they suspect the note may have been planted. A murder case has been registered.The woman, a second-year BCom student of Kalindi College, was found unconscious on a bed at Hotel Joya on Tuesday. The man she had checked in with lives directly opposite her house in Kureshipur village. Police are now searching for him.The sequence began on Monday morning, when she left home saying she was going to college. Her family remained in touch with her over phone till around 3pm, after which her mobile was switched off. When she did not return and repeated calls went unanswered, her family lodged a missing person’s complaint at Dhauj police station on Tuesday morning.A few hours later, cops at Sarai Khwaja police station informed the family that a woman had been found dead in a hotel room. They rushed there and identified her.Hotel staff told police that the two had checked in around 11am on Monday, submitting their own identity documents.The neighbour allegedly left during the night, while the student remained in the room. On Tuesday, staff knocked on the door to enquire if she would check out, but received no response. They then alerted police.The recovery of the handwritten note has added another layer to the case. Police said it mentioned pending monetary transactions. “Whatever is mine, Ankit will own it after me,” the note read, referring to the student’s brother.However, an officer said the handwriting did not appear to be hers and police suspected the note had been written by the neighbour to mislead them. Its origin and contents are being examined.The officer said the neighbour’s family runs a transport business, owning four to five trucks. Both his parents had died, and he frequently visited the student’s house and sometimes stayed there. Her parents run a grocery shop in the village.An FIR was registered under Section 103 of BNS (murder), besides the missing person’s case, at Dhauj police station. The body was sent to BK Hospital. The cause of death is yet to be established.“The autopsy will be carried out on Wednesday. The exact cause of death will be known only after the report is available,” the officer said.
Article Summary: The woman, a second-year BCom student of Kalindi College, was found unconscious on a bed at Hotel Joya. Police found a bottle of rat poison and a handwritten note in the room. The man she had checked in with lives directly opposite her house in Kureshipur village.

Article Title: 'Why wasn't it flagged earlier?': Hours before UK flight, CJP's Saurav Das stopped at IGI over passport 'discrepancy'
Article Text:
Saurav Das was prevented from traveling to the UK as his passport was flagged by immigration authorities.





New Delhi: A day after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das 's passport was flagged by immigration authorities at IGI airport and he was stopped from travelling to UK, Das said he was issued a show-cause notice alleging discrepancies in his passport only 5 hours before his flight at 1am Tuesday.Das said the notice cited discrepancies in his place-of-birth details.Addressing a news conference, Das said he was headed to UK for a series of engagements, including a panel discussion organised by Oxford Union, a debating society that is not run by Oxford University but has many students and alumni from the institution as members. The notice, according to Das, asked him to explain within seven days why his passport should not be impounded.At the news meet alongside CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh and national joint secretary Balkrishna Shukla, Das said he received the notice Monday while he was on his way to the airport. He said he could not see the communication at the time. He said the notice referred to alleged inputs about discrepancies in his passport concerning his place of birth but did not elaborate the grounds on which these inputs were being considered.Das questioned why the issue had not been flagged earlier, pointing out that his passport was issued in 2019, after police verification. He said he had undertaken several international trips since then. “How was I issued the passport which was given after police verification?” he asked.Alleging that the action was linked to his association with CJP, Das said, “I was scheduled to talk in various prestigious universities in London on their invitation. That trip couldn’t be completed because the coward govt has flagged my passport citing some discrepancies...”The Oxford Union panel discussion was scheduled for Dec 1, for which Das and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke were listed as key panellists on the organisation’s website.Das also listed Cambridge University, London School of Economics and University of Edinburgh among the institutions where he was scheduled to speak. He said some of the engagements were being organised independently by student groups, while others were being held with the knowledge of the universities. Das said he intended to explain the growth of the movement and how it gained traction through non-violent means. “The Indian students studying there wanted to understand what CJP movement is and how it grew. I would have spoken about how this movement without violence could become successful. How the world’s Gen Z could learn from us,” he said.Ratna Singh said she was also scheduled to travel to UK for the panel discussion but her visa was rejected a few days earlier. Dipke said he, too, had received an invitation but it was decided that Das would attend the UK engagement while he travelled to Nagpur for a CJP programme and demonstration on Nov 26, coinciding with Constitution Day.Questioning the action against Das, Dipke pointed to the cases of fugitive economic offenders Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi. “Is he (Das) a terrorist, a criminal? Why was he stopped?” Dipke asked at a separate news conference.LSESU Amnesty International Society issued a statement saying its event featuring Das had been indefinitely postponed. It condemned what it said was an “arbitrary obstruction” and the “apparent targeting of an individual seeking to engage in academic dialogue and public discussion”. The society expressed solidarity with Das and said it would share updates if the event could be rescheduled. TOI also reached out to Oxford Union for a comment but did not receive a response.
Article Summary: CJP co-convener Saurav Das was prevented from traveling to the UK as his passport was flagged by immigration authorities. Das said he was issued a show- cause notice alleging discrepancies in his passport only 5 hours before his flight at 1am Tuesday.

Article Title: Pakistani Netflix series starring Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan faces opposition in India, AICWA urges PM Modi to stop December 4 release
Article Text:
The All India Cine Workers Association has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding a Netflix series.





MUMBAI: The All India Cine Workers Association has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding a stop to the India release of upcoming Pakistani series 'Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' on Netflix on Dec 4.AICWA has sought a permanent ban on all Pakistani content in India."The cast of the series includes Fawad Khan , Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir and Saman Ansari, along with other Pakistani artistes, some of whom have spoken against India during times of tension... These are people of a terrorist country who will never wish well for India," the letter says.The association claims it had "banned" Pakistani artistes from working in India after the Pulwama attack. "After the Pahalgam attack, the Indian govt also imposed restrictions on Pakistani artistes and content. On May 8, 2025, the ministry of I&B issued an advisory asking all OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries in India to stop streaming Pakistani-origin content including web series, songs, podcasts. .. Releasing this series goes against the spirit of that advisory." AICWA president Suresh Gupta demanded a "strict law and penalties" for showing Pakistani content in India and appealed to Netflix and other streaming platforms to state on social media they would not show their programmes.
Article Summary: AICWA has sought a permanent ban on all Pakistani content in India. The cast of the series includes Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir and Saman Ansari. The association claims it had "banned" Pakistani artistes from working in India after the Pulwama attack.

Article Title: UP woman escapes hotel after night of assault, ex-boyfriend catches her, drags her back in crowded market
Article Text:
A 24-year-old woman escaped a hotel in Meerut where her ex-boyfriend confined and assaulted her.





MEERUT: A 24-year-old woman allegedly escaped from a hotel room in Meerut on Tuesday but was caught by her former boyfriend, who tried to drag her back. The incident, which took place in the busy Abu Lane market, was captured on CCTV.The accused, identified as Mohd Salman, allegedly chased the woman, caught hold of her and attempted to take her back to the hotel. He fled across the rooftop after police reached the spot following alerts from passersby.According to police, the woman, a resident of Vasundhara in Ghaziabad, had known Salman, a resident of Jainpur village in Meerut's Rohta area, for around two-and-a-half years. The two were previously in a relationship. Her family has recently arranged her marriage elsewhere.The woman told police that she had visited a friend in Mohkampur on Monday. While she was returning to Ghaziabad later that night, Salman allegedly took her to a hotel on Abu Lane, assaulted her and confined her to a room overnight. He also snatched her phone, which he returned later, she alleged.In her FIR, registered on Tuesday night, the woman stated: "Salman was my boyfriend a year ago.On Monday, I came to meet a friend in Mohkampur. While I was returning to Ghaziabad at night, Salman took me from my friend's place to a hotel, thrashed me and confined me there. He even snatched away my phone, though he returned it later. I escaped on Tuesday afternoon, but he caught hold of me, threatened me and then fled."Salman has been booked under sections 115(2), 127(2) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful confinement and criminal intimidation."A man and a woman had checked into a hotel. Following an argument, violence broke out between them. The woman told us that she had known the youth for the past two-and-a-half years and clarified that she had not been abducted. Teams have been constituted based on her complaint, and strict action will be taken against the accused," said Circle Officer (Sadar) Sanjay Gupta.Police have sealed the hotel and formed two teams, including the SWAT unit, to conduct raids and apprehend Salman.
Article Summary: A 24-year-old woman escaped from a hotel room in Meerut on Tuesday but was caught by her former boyfriend, who tried to drag her back. The accused, identified as Mohd Salman, allegedly chased the woman and attempted to take her back to the hotel. He fled across the rooftop after police reached the spot following alerts from passersby.

Article Title: After Mumbai unit's Rs 1 lakh offer, Pimpri Chinchwad Shiv Sena (UBT) announces cash reward for slapping Shaina NC
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions

Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph

Poll Vote & Share your view How should political disputes like this be addressed? Through peaceful dialogue Through legal action Through public protests 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Similarly, we, as the Pimpri Chinchwad unit of Shiv Sena (UBT), announce a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps her," Pawar said.The controversy erupted on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Mumbai to protest against references to Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.During the protest, party leaders tore pages from the book. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their sentiments, while insisting that she had no intention of disrespecting him.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions. Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackersay and Eknath Shinde.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'

Death sentence and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: ‘Hardest meeting of my life’: Jensen Huang apologises to Nvidia staff after CEO comeback
Article Text:
Huang also sought to reassure women employees, describing himself as 'one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women.'

Huang says he is undergoing therapy

Nvidia CEO promises regular performance reviews

Huang rejects claims of preferential treatment

Why Huang stepped down and returned as Nvidia CEO

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct and admitted making “very serious personal mistakes” during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the top post. Huang acknowledged that his personal behaviour had hurt his family and wife. He also promised to hold himself to higher standards and undergo regular performance reviews based on feedback from employees.“This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang said, according to a report by The Wired. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”Addressing employees, Huang said he had been attending therapy sessions every day for an hour and a half. He added that the sessions had been helping him.“I made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife,” he said.Huang also stressed that Nvidia's code of conduct remained applicable to everyone in the company, including its top leadership. He said he had written much of the code himself and that it was designed to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”He warned that violations would not be tolerated. However, he clarified that every violation would not automatically lead to an employee's dismissal.“But that does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would determine the action taken.Huang also addressed criticism of his intense management style and acknowledged that his behaviour had sometimes affected employees negatively.While he maintained that his demanding approach helped push people to perform better, he admitted that he sometimes went too far.“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang said.He said he needed to find a way to maintain his commitment to Nvidia without hurting the people working for him.“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” he said.Huang also announced that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review. The process would involve seeking feedback from people working with him, potentially as often as once a month.He said he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and did not intend to introduce the practice across the company.The CEO also pushed back against suggestions that he had been reinstated because of his standing in the technology industry.“There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang said.He rejected the suggestion that his position gave him special treatment or placed him above Nvidia's code of conduct.Huang also sought to reassure women employees, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women”.He highlighted the company's flexible work policies, saying they allowed employees to build their families while pursuing their careers.“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” he said.He further sought to reassure employees about the company's ability to function without him, saying his brief absence had demonstrated its operational strength.“I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang said.Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation earlier this month following concerns about his personal conduct and lack of candour. The development came after media reports about alleged extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman accused of having links to Chinese intelligence services.However, the same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days after accepting his resignation. The decision followed fresh assurances from Huang and information from the Trump administration that he was not under federal scrutiny.His return has drawn mixed reactions within Nvidia. While some employees welcomed the decision, others reportedly remain concerned about his conduct and the board's move to reinstate him.The controversy has also led to continued legal and regulatory scrutiny. Nvidia's board is investigating whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. US lawmakers are also expecting him to testify before Congress next week.Meanwhile, lawsuits and other investigations are ongoing into the company's disclosures about Huang's conduct and its compliance with US export controls on chips.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang apologised to employees on Tuesday for violating the company's code of conduct. He admitted making'very serious personal mistakes' during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the top post. Huang acknowledged that his personal behaviour had hurt his family and wife. He also promised to hold himself to higher standards and undergo regular performance reviews based on feedback from employees.

Article Title: How Jensen Huang's Silicon Valley friends ran a 'war room' to get him back as Nvidia CEO
Article Text:
Marc Andreessen, Travis Kalanick, and Nvidia investors built a 'war room' to bring back Jensen Huang

Jensen Huang's allies began lobbying within hours of his resignation

A 45-minute call with JD Vance took Huang's case to the White House

Nvidia's board took Jensen Huang back after a secret Sunday meeting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia's chief executive just 11 days after he resigned. The push that got him there started with a small circle of friends in Silicon Valley. Tech founders and investors set up what one of them called a "war room", lobbied Nvidia's board in public and in private, and then pulled in President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance , the Financial Times reported.Nvidia's board voted unanimously on November 23 to reinstate Huang. Six days earlier, board chair Harvey Jones had said the company did not intend to bring him back. Huang stepped down on November 12 after reports of two affairs. One was with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. US officials believe she was a Chinese intelligence asset. The other was with a subordinate.Nvidia shares jumped more than 30% on Monday, the biggest one-day gain in market value on record for a US company, according to The Wall Street Journal.According to the FT, the group included Uber founder Travis Kalanick, investors Gavin Baker, Brad Gerstner and Marc Andreessen, and Goldman Sachs executive John Underwood. Within 24 hours, Baker and Gerstner, both large Nvidia shareholders, published an open letter asking the board to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".The effort had Huang's backing, the FT reported. Publicly, Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney threw their weight behind a "Bring Jensen Back" letter.A letter calling for his return gathered more than 200,000 signatures, the WSJ reported, and employees signing it warned of "irreplaceable talent loss".One of the allies arranged a 45-minute phone call between Huang and Vance last week. Huang used it to defend his views on US export controls, remote access to chips and his Megaspeed dealings, the FT said.Trump stepped in after returning from China at the end of last week. He asked Vance to talk to Huang and work with the board, The New York Times reported. Vance set out to get the board two things it needed: an assurance that the administration did not see Huang as a national security threat, and a statement that he was not facing criminal charges.The WSJ reported that Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vance on Saturday that Huang was not the target or subject of any Justice Department investigation. Over the next 48 hours, Trump, Vance and other officials relayed that to board members.Trump told the WSJ he reached the board "in numerous ways" and "through representatives", and that the falling stock made his job easier. "The climate became more and more right as the company stock began to tumble," he told the paper. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had earlier called for a leadership shake-up at Nvidia. He softened his stance over the weekend.The talks were so secretive that interim CEO Colette Kress was kept out, the FT reported. During a long board session on Sunday, Huang disclosed affairs beyond the two already reported and came across as sorry for them, according to the WSJ. After conversations about candour, the board decided his return was the best path.On Monday, Huang walked into Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters to cheering staff. "I'm terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this," he said. At an all-hands meeting on Tuesday, he told employees he was in therapy for 90 minutes a day. He called the idea that Trump pressured the board "completely untrue", the NYT reported.Even after the rally, Nvidia is worth about a fifth less than it was a month ago, the FT noted. Nvidia and Huang still face FBI and SEC probes, plus congressional investigations. Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter have been summoned to hearings in Washington next week.The board says its internal investigation will continue and that Nvidia will hire a chief compliance officer. On Monday, the US Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang's allies began lobbying within hours of his resignation. A 45-minute call with JD Vance took Huang's case to the White House. Nvidia's board voted unanimously on November 23 to reinstate Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12 after reports of two affairs.

Article Title: In address to jatha from India, Pak PM’s son calls for dialogue, reopening of Kartarpur Corridor
Article Text:
Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif’s son Hamza speaks at an event in Lahore to mark Guru Nanak Dev’s Parkash Purb

Nankana Sahib





: Calling for India and Pakistan to move beyond hostility through dialogue, former Pakistan Punjab chief minister Hamza Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said borders could divide land but not culture, love and relationships.He also called for reopening the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, assuring Sikh pilgrims that Pakistan would welcome them with open arms.Addressing the sangat on the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, Hamza, the eldest son of Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , conveyed greetings on behalf of the PM and Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz. He urged the two countries to resolve their differences through mutual respect and tolerance.Referring to tensions between Iran and the US, he said dialogue could achieve what weapons could not. “Cannons and artillery cannot achieve what a few words of love can,” he said, recalling former Indian PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee ’s visit to Pakistan as an expression of goodwill.Hamza said the presence of the sangat reminded him of his grandfather, Mian Muhammad Sharif, who often spoke about Amritsar and the family’s ancestral village, Jati Umra.Recalling his visit to the village, he said, “I feel as if I am addressing members of my own family.”He said Guru Nanak Dev’s message of love, equality, service and humanity remained relevant across the world. Reflecting on his 25 years in politics, he said the most important lesson he had learnt was the Sikh guru’s teaching of Vand Chhako — sharing what one earns.He claimed that minorities in Pakistan enjoyed equal rights and urged Sikhs to visit historic gurdwaras there. He assured the sangat that difficulties faced by pilgrims would be addressed and said future generations should carry forward Guru Nanak Dev’s message of peace.The remarks were shared by a Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee official accompanying the jatha led by officiating Akal Takht jathedar Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargajj in Pakistan.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan Punjab chief minister Hamza Shehbaz Sharif called for reopening the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor. He urged the two countries to resolve their differences through mutual respect and tolerance. Hamza said the presence of the sangat reminded him of his grandfather, Mian Muhammad Sharif, who often spoke about Amritsar.

Article Title: One name, many birthdays? Chennai RPO re-checks CJP's Saurav Das's papers after Aadhaar, passport mismatch
Article Text:
Saurav Das has encountered passport complications following discrepancies in his birth details among multiple documents





NEW DELHI: Discrepancies in Saurav Das ’s birth details across his Aadhaar, passport and birth certificate have prompted the Chennai Regional Passport Office (RPO) to initiate a fresh verification of his documents and passport records, sources said.Das has been asked to explain the alleged discrepancies and cannot use his passport for international travel until the matter is resolved.An email notice sent to him on Monday evening gave him seven days to respond to allegations of “material suppression of facts” regarding his place of birth. He has been asked to submit supporting documents clarifying the “incorrect” particulars. Failure to do so could lead to his passport being impounded under Section 10(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. The notice also advised him not to use the passport until he submits his response.Passport authorities can order re-verification even after a passport has been issued if incorrect or adverse information comes to light during its validity. The RPO can issue a show-cause notice asking the holder why the passport should not be impounded.“As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to a passport holder over furnishing incorrect particulars and a reply is awaited, the person cannot travel abroad on that passport until the matter is disposed of,” an officer told TOI.“Das was aware that the pending RPO notice would be flagged in the immigration system, preventing him from boarding his flight to London. Yet, he chose to travel to the airport, possibly so he could play the victim after being stopped at immigration,” the officer alleged.Das reportedly claimed he did not see the email, which was sent hours before his scheduled flight, until he checked his inbox at the immigration counter.Another officer said Das has until November 30 to respond. “Let him satisfy the RPO as to which set of birth documents must be relied on. Once the RPO clears him in the re-verification exercise, he can resume international travel on the same passport,” the officer said.Sources said discrepancies had been flagged in Das’s date of birth and father's name across documents, including Aadhaar, passport and school certificates issued in different places where he had lived, including Delhi and Puducherry.Meanwhile, a PIL has been filed in the Madras High Court alleging inconsistencies in his birth and parentage documents and questioning his citizenship.
Article Summary: Das has been asked to explain the alleged discrepancies and cannot use his passport for international travel until the matter is resolved. A PIL has been filed in the Madras High Court alleging inconsistencies in his birth and parentage documents and questioning his citizenship.

Article Title: ‘Observation home is a child reformative centre’: Juvenile Justice Board denies teen driver bail in fatal crash that killed Mumbai biker, grievously injured his wife
Article Text: MUMBAI: The Juvenile Justice Board on Saturday rejected the fresh bail plea of a 17-year-old driver who allegedly rammed his car into the scooter of a 33-year-old Ghatkopar businessman, Dhrumil Patel, killing him and grievously injuring his wife, 32-year-old teacher Menal Patel in Feb this year.The board further said, “An Observation Home established and registered under Section 47 is statutorily entrusted with the functions of temporary reception, care, rehabilitation and social integration of children in conflict with law. Therefore, an observation home is a child reformative centre during pendency of inquiry.”On Feb 5, 2026, the couple were heading back to Ghatkopar from Parel, where Dhrumil worked, on his scooter when a car from the opposite direction “violently struck them”, the appeal said. Dhrumil sustained grievous head injuries, rib fractures and fractures to his left knee and right wrist, while Menal too broke her right hand and sustained grievous injuries to her right eye and other parts.The minor had argued that the investigation was complete, the chargesheet had been filed, no custodial recovery was pending, and the social investigation material did not show substance abuse, criminal background or psychological disorder.The plea also said the minor had completed the 12th board examination in commerce with 74.83% marks and had taken admission to a Bachelor of Commerce course at College of Commerce, making continued institutional custody disruptive to higher education.The defence also disputed allegations linked to social media material and an alleged sighting in Ghatkopar. The minor denied deleting the common Instagram account and said the chargesheet attributed the deletion of the common account to another minor. The defence also said the alleged sighting near Somaiya College did not establish a breach of the earlier bail condition because the condition barred residence in Ghatkopar or Chembur, not temporary presence or passage through the area.After the chargesheet was filed—including allegations under Section 238 BNS over deleted social media and stunt material—the sessions court set aside the minor’s earlier bail and directed his placement in a Child Reformative Centre, a move affirmed by Bombay High Court after an exam-related stay and subsequent appearances before the board. Following the High Court’s rejection, the minor was not produced on initial dates promised by his father while police checked the Koperkhairane premises, before a written notice of surrender was given and he appeared with his parents. He then filed a fresh bail plea which was rejected.The prosecution opposed the bail plea, saying the offence was serious and the earlier bail order had already been cancelled by superior courts. The prosecution argued that release might expose the minor to known criminals, create a possibility of similar conduct, and lead to absconding or pressure on witnesses.The survivor victim also opposed the application, calling the plea an attempt to reopen issues already considered by the Sessions Court and Bombay High Court. The survivor also pointed to the minor’s non-availability after the sessions court order, the father’s failure to produce him on dates allegedly promised to police, and the eventual production only 10 days after the high court order.The board referred to Bombay High Court’s earlier observations, quoting, “The applicant would be exposed to moral, physical and psychological danger due to lack of parental control. He may again indulge in the stunt act with his friends causing danger to others. It will defeat ends of justice.”The board held that no substantial change in circumstances had been shown after the earlier bail order was set aside by the Sessions Court and the challenge was rejected by Bombay High Court.HC had also recorded concerns about stunt videos and parental control. The Board reproduced the High Court’s finding that the juvenile “was not only reckless about his own safety but also that of the others around him” and that the material showed the juvenile “was in the habit of boasting about his acts.” The High Court had further observed that “keeping him in reformative home would make him understand gravity of his act. ”
Article Summary: The Juvenile Justice Board on Saturday rejected the fresh bail plea of a 17-year-old driver who allegedly rammed his car into the scooter of a Ghatkopar businessman. The minor had argued that the investigation was complete, the chargesheet had been filed, no custodial recovery was pending, and the social investigation material did not show substance abuse.

Article Title: ​​Traffic police cancel faulty e-challans issued to two members of the same family in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

TOI





Maharashtra traffic police have cancelled e-challans issued to two members of the same family from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar after errors in the issuance of challans came to light.After the matter was raised in areport, the cops cancelled the challans and sent confirmation messages to both brothers on their mobile numbers.Assistant Commissioner of Police (traffic), Subhash Bhujang, said an explanation has been sought from traffic cops on duty who issued e-challans. “After receiving an explanation in both cases, we will take future course of action, if needed,” he said.Nityanand Zadbuke, the car owner who was wrongly fined due to the misplacement of a letter on the vehicle registration plate, said he was highly relieved. “I was slapped with a fine of Rs 1,000 even though I was not at fault. The govt should bring necessary reforms in its system to avoid incidents of wrong e-challans,” he said.His elder brother, Dr Amol, who was wrongly fined Rs 2,000, also underlined the need for reforms in the e-challan system. “The grievance redressal platform of the e-challan needs to undergo reform.It should be made more pro-citizen and must factor in versions of citizens,” he said.In Dr Amol’s case, he was issued an e-challan in December last year for not wearing a helmet while riding a scooter. When the dispute was raised through the grievance redressal forum, the challan had modified the offence ​as “speeding” at 57 Km/hr even though the vehicle was within the speed limit.

Article Title: ​​​Two killed, 17 injured as Nagpur-Mumbai bus overturns on Samruddhi Expressway
Article Text:
A private passenger bus that met with accident on the Samruddhi Expressway in Phulambri taluka in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Monday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two passengers were killed and 17 others were injured after a private passenger bus overturned on the Samruddhi Expressway at Naygaon in Phulambri taluka of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in the early hours of Monday.The deceased are Raghunandan Datta Sangale (26), a resident of West Mumbai, and Vinod Uttam Jadhav, a resident of Ghonsgaon in Yavatmal’s Arni taluka, who died during treatment.The accident occurred around 1.10 am on Monday at Channel No. 426 on the expressway’s Nagpur-Mumbai corridor, as the bus driver is suspected to have dozed off during the journey, said Sonali Paikrao, in charge of Phulambri police station.“The bus, MH-41-ZH-9955, was travelling from Nagpur to Mumbai with 38 passengers. As per preliminary information, the driver dozed off, lost control of the vehicle and the bus overturned on the highway, leaving several passengers injured,” Paikrao said, adding that the case registration process against the bus driver was underway.On receiving information about the accident, highway police and a Phulambri police station team rushed to the spot and coordinated the rescue operation. Local rescue teams, ambulances and police safely pulled the passengers from the bus and shifted the injured to Govt Medical College and Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for treatment.Police have appealed to drivers on the Samruddhi Expressway to start their journey only after adequate rest, avoid driving when feeling sleepy or tired, follow speed limits and give top priority to passenger safety.
Article Summary: The accident occurred around 1.10 am on Monday at Channel No. 426 on the expressway’s Nagpur-Mumbai corridor. The bus driver is suspected to have dozed off during the journey. The deceased are Raghunandan Datta Sangale (26), a resident of West Mumbai, and Vinod Uttam Jadhav, who died during treatment.

Article Title: BJP corporator’s minor son booked after speeding SUV kills Beed couple; police say friend was driving
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The minor son of a BJP corporator was booked after a speeding SUV allegedly rammed a motorcycle head-on, killing a couple in Beed’s Majalgaon on Nov 20. Police, however, said a video shot inside the SUV shows the corporator’s son was not driving.The victims, Prahlad Gaikwad and his wife Sunita Gaikwad, were residents of Mangrul village near Majalgaon. According to a complaint filed by the couple’s son, the two were returning home on their motorcycle after attending a shraddha ceremony. Around 3.30 pm, near Saubhagya Mangal Karyalaya, an SUV allegedly came at high speed and hit their motorcycle head-on.Police subsequently booked the minor son of a local corporator under sections 106(1), 281 and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and sections 134 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act. However, police said fresh evidence that emerged during the investigation indicates that the corporator’s son was not behind the wheel.Majalgaon police station in-charge Dhananjay Dhone said a video filmed inside the SUV, apparently for a reel, shows four friends in the vehicle before the crash.“It shows four friends inside the car, with the corporator’s son sitting next to his friend who was driving. The video also shows the airbags deploying after the impact. The corporator’s son was not driving. His friend was behind the wheel,” Dhone said.A section of local residents alleged that the crash was linked to road rage and illegal street racing. Police said that allegation has not been established.“The CCTV footage of the accident shows the SUV was at high speed. It is not yet clear whether any street racing was on,” Dhone said.Police are recording statements of those involved. No arrests had been made till Monday evening.The BJP corporator, meanwhile, also denied that his son was driving or that the SUV was involved in street racing. “My son’s friend was driving the car and he appeared before the police after the accident. My political rivals are trying to target me and my family after the accident,” he said.
Article Summary: The minor son of a BJP corporator was booked after a speeding SUV allegedly rammed a motorcycle head-on, killing a couple. Police, however, said a video shot inside the SUV shows the corporator’s son was not driving. A section of local residents alleged that the crash was linked to road rage and illegal street racing. Police said that allegation has not been established.

Article Title: ​Police’s own photos expose wrong e-challans issued to same family in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two separate incidents in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar have exposed acts of wrongful challans issued by the traffic police against members of the same family.In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued the same challan for overspeeding, even though the police speed camera showed the car was within limits.In both cases, the police’s own photographs contradict their challans, yet both fines still stand against two members of the same family from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The first case is of a car, MH20-EY0545. An e-challan was issued against the car’s owner on Saturday for using a mobile phone while driving. However, the photograph attached as proof shows a completely different vehicle — MH20-EA0545. The difference is of one letter — Y in place of A — in the number of both cars.“I was shocked to see a message on my mobile about a traffic violation when I had not even driven the car on Saturday,” said Nityanand Zadbuke, the car owner.The second incident involved Nityanand’s elder brother, Dr Amol Zadbuke, a health professional.The owner of car number MH20-CH3609 had first received an e-challan for not wearing a helmet in Dec last year. “I was taken aback by the traffic violation. When I raised a dispute, the same challan issued last year was shown as proof of overspeeding. But police’s own speed-camera photo shows my vehicle was moving at 57 Km/hr, which is well within the permissible speed of 95 Km/ hr,” Dr Zadbuke said.When contacted, Subhash Bhujang, the assistant commissioner of police (traffic), said that complaints related to both e-challans would be examined if vehicle owners approach the traffic police.“Misreading of letters on a number plate by the technical system cannot be ruled out, as vehicles are constantly moving. The other case with Dr Zadbuke is exceptional, and official intervention will be offered if the vehicle owner is not happy with the earlier grievance redressal,” he said.
Article Summary: In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued same challan for overspeeding.

Article Title: ​​10,767km, 3 states later, rare vulture makes first recorded halt in Maharashtra's Latur
Article Text:
Critically endangered the Indian vulture seen in Ausa taluka of Latur district-

More than just a rare sighting





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A seven-year-old female Indian vulture, released into the wild at Melghat Tiger Reserve, made a halt in Latur’s Ausa taluka after clocking 10,767 km, marking the first recorded sighting of the critically endangered species in the district.It had flown thousands of kilometres across three states, crossed forests and open landscapes and even ventured into Karnataka. Then, on Nov 18, the vulture stopped in Latur.The bird is no anonymous visitor. A yellow ring on its left leg carries the tag F14. A blue one on its right reads M99. A tracking device on its back has allowed Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) to follow its remarkable journey.The vulture was bred at BNHS’s vulture breeding centre at Pinjore in Haryana. It was later released in the Somthana forest range of Melghat along with 15 other Indian vultures.Its brief Latur stop created excitement among local birders. Wildlife enthusiast Abhijit Rasal alerted Latur-based wildlife lover Dhananjay Gutte on the night of Nov 18. Before dawn, Gutte, deputy conservator of forests (Social Forestry) Amitraj Jadhav and local birder Datta Ambekar headed to the roosting site.They reached at 5.30 am and waited.“After spending some time, we spotted the vulture perched on a tree. We photographed and videographed it. The bird appeared healthy and was moving naturally in the wild,” Gutte said.The visitor did not stay for long. At 8.40 am, it took off again. It later reached Murbad taluka in Thane district.From Melghat to MP, Karnataka and back. The Latur halt is only one chapter in F14/M99’s long journey.Abhijeet Das, project biologist with BNHS’s Vulture Project Maharashtra, said the bird initially remained close to its release site in Melghat. “After its release, F14/M99 stayed near the site, learning to forage and building its flight muscles. It dispersed from the release site on May 28, crossing Maharashtra and reaching Madhya Pradesh. It used several landscapes known to support wild vulture populations,” Das said.Then came an observation that conservationists consider particularly significant. On Sept 18, F14/M99 was spotted near Halali dam in Madhya Pradesh. It was roosting with wild vultures. More importantly, it had a full crop, indicating it had fed successfully.“This provides the first evidence that the released birds are capable of independent foraging and integrating with the wild population,” Das said.For a bird bred in captivity and released into the wild, those two things matter enormously: finding its own food and finding its place among wild vultures.Das said the traveller returned to Maharashtra on Nov 13.“The bird entered Maharashtra again on Nov 13, crossing Akot and Malkapur and reaching Nashik, Thane and Pune. It then travelled south to near Vijayapura in Karnataka. It returned to Maharashtra on Nov 18, taking a route through Latur, and reached Thane again on Nov 20,” he said.The Indian vulture (Gyps indicus) is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List. The species performs one of nature’s least glamorous but most vital jobs. Vultures rapidly dispose of animal carcasses, helping keep the landscape clean and limiting opportunities for disease to spread.India once had vast populations of vultures. Their numbers crashed dramatically, with experts largely linking the decline to the veterinary use of diclofenac. That makes every successfully released bird important.And every sign that a captive-bred vulture can survive, feed and move naturally in the wild adds another piece to the conservation puzzle.For Gutte, however, F14/M99’s journey has also put Latur on the vulture map. He said the district’s first recorded sighting was encouraging for conservation and raised hopes that its landscape could offer suitable habitat for vultures.F14/M99, meanwhile, has already moved on. Its Latur visit lasted barely a morning. But after 10,767 km in the wild, one night’s halt was enough to leave behind a first for the district.
Article Summary: A seven-year-old female Indian vulture, released into the wild at Melghat Tiger Reserve, made a halt in Latur’s Ausa taluka. It had flown thousands of kilometres across three states, crossed forests and open landscapes and even ventured into Karnataka. A tracking device on its back has allowed Bombay Natural History Society to follow its remarkable journey.

Article Title: Ladki Bahin has strained Maharashtra finances, but can’t step back from it: Narhari Zirwal
Article Text:
The programme, launched ahead of the 2024 assembly elections, provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.

Ladkya Bahini





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Food and drug administration minister Narhari Zirwal on Saturday acknowledged that the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme has put Maharashtra govt in a difficult financial position, with drought now adding to the strain on the state’s finances.Speaking at a public event in Loha during a tour of Nanded district , Zirwal said govt could not step back from the flagship welfare scheme despite the burden it had created. “Nobody told us before the election to launch the scheme, but we made many(beloved sisters). Now, we cannot distance ourselves from them,” Zirwal said.He described the state’s financial position as “strained” because of the scheme. “To add to it, we now have a drought,” he said.His remarks are significant as they amount to a rare acknowledgement from within the state cabinet of the fiscal pressure created by the Ladki Bahin scheme. The programme, launched ahead of the 2024 assembly elections, provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.Zirwal said the drought would require substantial additional spending, particularly if the water crisis worsens. “The 1972 drought caused a shortage of food.This time, we have a water shortage. We may even have to arrange water through planes or trains, and such measures will require huge funds,” he said.The NCP politician, however, said govt would ensure there was no shortage of resources in tackling the drought.His remarks come days after deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said on Nov 9 that govt would take a decision at an appropriate time on increasing the monthly Ladki Bahin assistance from Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,100. Shinde and chief minister Devendra Fadnavis have repeatedly maintained that the scheme will continue.Zirwal also raised eyebrows with a separate remark that “NCP’s clock is not keeping accurate time”, referring to the party’s election symbol. He later sought to clarify the remark. “When Ajit Dada was alive, all public functions started on time because he was very punctual. Now, programmes sometimes get delayed. My comment was made only in that context,” he said.
Article Summary: Food and drug administration minister Narhari Zirwal acknowledged that the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme has put Maharashtra govt in a difficult financial position. He described the state’s financial position as ‘strained’ because of the scheme. The programme provides eligible women Rs 1,500 a month.
